text: Rama was a prince of Ayodhya, heir to its throne, and known for keeping his word.
asr: Rama was a prince of Iodia, heir to its throne, and known for keeping his word.

text: To keep his father's promise, he gave up the crown and walked into the forest for fourteen years, with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana.
asr: To keep his father's promise, he gave up the crown and walked into the forest for 14 years, with his wife Sida and his brother Lakshmana.

text: There, a golden deer lured him away, and the demon king Ravana carried Sita off to his island, Lanka. As she flew, she dropped her jewels, to leave a trail.
Searching for her, Rama found friends: an army of monkeys, and Hanuman, who leapt across the sea to find her.
Then the army built a bridge of floating stones, each one marked with Rama's name.
In the battle that followed, Ravana fell, and Sita was free at last.
asr: In the battle that followed, Ravana fell, and Sito was free at last.

text: When they came home, the people lit their way with lamps. Many still do, every autumn, at Diwali.
Rama: the one who kept his word.
